title: The parts import never changes an entry's part number
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test with its part number in capital letters, Min 1, Max 5 and 3 in bin location A.
  • Have a parts import file with one row whose part number is part A's number in small letters, with a new description, description 2, Min 2, Max 8, quantity 3 and bin location A, so the row matches part A.
  • Start on the Inventory data import page (Settings, then Data Import, then Inventory).
custom_steps:
1. Upload the file.
  2. Run the import.
  3. Click Parts in the top bar.
  4. Click Inventory in the left menu.
  5. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  6. Click Part Library in the left menu.
  7. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The file is ready to import.

Step 2:

  • The import finishes and does not refuse the row.

Step 3:

  • The Parts left menu shows Inventory.

Step 4:

  • The Inventory page opens.

Step 5:

  • Still one row for part A: its Part Number still reads part A's number in capital letters, not the small-letter number from the file.
  • It now shows Min 2, Max 8 and description 2: the row updated this part, with 3 in bin location A.

Step 6:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 7:

  • One entry is listed, with part A's number unchanged in capital letters.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog), story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description)

  • S13-N9: “The parts CSV import never moves a part to a different Part Library entry and never changes an entry's part number.”
  • S7-N7: “S7-N3 to S7-N6 do not apply to the parts CSV import. An import row whose number matches a part already stocked at this location updates that part (S13-N9a). It is never refused for a duplicate number.”
  • Feature Overview, Out of scope: “How the parts CSV import matches a part number to a Part Library entry. The import matches a number ignoring upper and lower case. If nothing matches, it also ignores hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces. It writes the row's description onto the entry it matches. It never moves a part to a different entry and never changes an entry's part number (S13-N9).”

From: Product's answers (Chris Ward, 9 Oct and 14 Oct 2026, saved in po-answers-2026-10-09/ and po-answers-2026-10-14/), read 27 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 14 Oct 2026, answer 3 b: “b) No. The duplicate check doesn't apply to the import. A matching number updates the part already stocked at the location and is never refused (S7-N7).”
